specification.problem: Build an exact oracle U_f|x>|y> = |x>|y xor f(x)> for an explicit Boolean truth table f on n bits, using a phase-polynomial (Walsh-Hadamard/Fourier parity) expansion, parity ancillas and Z rotations, with a constant-depth structure when fan-out is treated as an elementary gate.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Tiny instance n=2 and f=OR(x0,x1), with the target y included. The circuit uses explicit parities and RZ/phase gates with no black-box queries. The paper's general MBQC-equivalence proof, the exact constant-depth fan-out realisation and the optimised ancilla counts are outside this scope.

symbols.meaning: classical Boolean function given as a truth table
parity mask selecting a subset of input bits
parity of the selected bits, sum_i s_i x_i mod 2
phase-polynomial coefficient: the phase pi f(x) = sum_s alpha_s (s.x mod 2)

equations.label: Bit-flip oracle
equations.description: Target oracle for a classical function.
equations.abstract_quote: any quantum oracle implementing a classical function
equations.justification: The abstract says the oracle implements a classical function; the XOR form is the standard definition of such an oracle.
assumptions: f is an explicit truth table

equations.label: Phase oracle from bit-flip oracle
equations.latex: U_f=(I\otimes H)\,\Big(\sum_x |x\rangle\langle x|\otimes Z^{f(x)}\Big)(I\otimes H),\quad Z^{f(x)}=e^{i\pi f(x) Z_y\text{-conjugate}}
equations.description: The oracle equals Hadamards on y around a diagonal operator that applies Z to y exactly when f(x)=1. The Z on y is a phase (-1)^{f(x) y}.
equations.justification: Standard identity H Z H = X, applied conditionally on f(x).

equations.label: Phase polynomial of f*y
equations.description: Replace this with the exact-form expansion in eq_4. Each term is a parity of selected x bits and y, realised as a phase on a parity ancilla.
equations.justification: The sketch includes y in the parities. The exact general coefficients are computed classically from the truth table.
assumptions: coefficients computed classically from the truth table

equations.label: Walsh-Hadamard expansion of the integer phase
equations.description: Walsh-Hadamard expansion of the phase function. Realising it as a product of RZ rotations on parity ancillas requires the phase-polynomial form eq_5.
equations.justification: Standard Fourier analysis on the Boolean cube. Relation to the paper's method is not confirmed.

equations.label: Parity-sum form for the phase
equations.latex: f(x)=\sum_{s\ne 0}c_s\,(s\cdot x \bmod 2),\; c_s=\frac{(-1)^{|s|+1}}{2^{|s|-1}}\ \text{ real-valued, with } (s\cdot x\bmod 2)=\tfrac12(1-(-1)^{s\cdot x})
equations.description: Real-valued parity expansion of f. Each parity bit p_s(x)=(s.x mod 2) gets a phase exp(i pi c_s p_s). Exact c_s come from solving f(x)=sum_s c_s p_s(x), which is a 2^n-by-2^n invertible system after adding the constant term. The OR closed form shown is not claimed to be correct for every n.
equations.justification: The sketch states the Fourier expansion has 2^n-1 terms. The solution is reproducible by solving the linear system classically.
assumptions: solve the linear system numerically for the c_s

equations.label: Z-rotation on a parity ancilla
equations.latex: R_Z(\theta_s)=\mathrm{diag}(1,e^{i\theta_s}),\ \theta_s=\pi c_s,\ \text{applied to } a_s \text{ holding } s\cdot x
equations.description: A phase gate on each parity ancilla gives total phase exp(i pi sum_s c_s p_s(x)) = (-1)^{f(x)}.
equations.abstract_quote: arbitrary rotations along $Z$ axis and unbounded fan-outs are elementary operations
equations.justification: The abstract names Z rotations and fan-out as the elementary gates.

registers.name: y
registers.role: target; included in the parities for the controlled-Z-on-y step

registers.name: a
registers.size: 2^n-1 (3 for n=2) parity ancillas, or 2^(n+1)-1 if y is included

specification.initial_state: |x>|y>|0...0> for a computational basis input, or a superposition on x

steps.description: Classically compute the real coefficients c_s from the truth table of f.
Compute each parity s.x into ancilla a_s using CX gates (a fan-out of x_i to every ancilla whose mask contains i). For the controlled-on-y version, also include y in the masks.
Apply the phase gate with angle pi c_s on each ancilla a_s. In the controlled-on-y version use the parity of (s.x) xor y so the phase acts only as a Z-type kick on y.
Uncompute the parity ancillas with the same CX layers, then apply H on y.

specification.measurement: For counts, measure y and optionally x only. Qiskit is little-endian: with measure(i,i), bits[::-1][i] is classical bit i. Check that the ancillas are |0> from the statevector.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compare the measured y with y xor f(x) for each basis input, and check ancilla cleanliness.
assumptions: Smallest case n=2, f=OR chosen by us because no scope was given.
Fan-out is realised as CX gates, so simulated depth is not constant.
Ancilla count is exponential in n.
missing_information: Exact constant-depth fan-out and parity gate construction and its MBQC equivalence.
Exact formulation of the angle schedule for general f, in particular the controlled-on-y version, which the sketch leaves vague.
How the paper reaches an exact OR with its specific angles.
